Applied Materials

Automated RF Gasket Cutting Machine

RF gaskets were cut by hand against a tape measure. Accuracy depended on who was cutting. I built a machine that feeds stock to a set length and tells the operator when to cut.

A Raspberry Pi 5 runs the touchscreen interface and supervises an Arduino Mega motion controller. A NEMA 23 stepper drives the feed, and rotary encoders measure the length actually fed, so the machine stops on true length rather than step count.

  • Raspberry Pi 5
  • Arduino Mega
  • NEMA 23 stepper
  • Rotary encoders
  • Python / Tkinter
  • Arduino C++

Applied Materials

Automated O-Ring Cleaning Machine

A portable, cart-mounted machine that washes and dries O-rings on a repeatable cycle instead of by hand. An Arduino-based PLC sequences the cycle, driving stepper motion through the wash and dry stages and switching pumps and air through relay modules.

Deionized water runs through an inline filter for the wash, and a DI air knife handles the dry.

  • Arduino PLC
  • C++
  • Stepper drivers
  • Relay modules
  • DI water
  • Inline filtration
  • Air knife

20%Less material in redesigned support tubes, same stiffness

Nanoscale Design & Manufacturing Lab, UT Austin

Structural and thermal design for nanoscale manufacturing equipment

I redesigned the system's bolted solid support tubes as hollow sections. Bending stiffness depends mostly on material far from the center, so the change removed 20% of the material without giving up stiffness.

I also designed a copper heat sink in SolidWorks to replace an aluminum part. FEA showed a 6% thermal improvement, and I machined the final part myself on a CNC mill.

  • SolidWorks
  • Thermal FEA
  • Structural design
  • CNC machining
  • DFM

Academic project

Static structural FEA

A full static study on a three-bearing spinner assembly: meshing, fixtures, bearing-face loads, then reading the results. Peak stress concentrated at the bearing bores, and the minimum factor of safety came out at 1.4, which set where material could and could not come off.

  • SolidWorks Simulation
  • von Mises
  • Factor of safety
  • Mesh convergence
